universities.name: St. Peter's Institute of Higher Education and Research
universities.summary: St. Peter’s Institute of Higher Education and Research is a private deemed-to-be university at Avadi, Chennai. Its academic portfolio spans engineering, architecture, arts, sciences, commerce and management. Regular engineering degrees combine classroom study with practical, internship and project work. Chennai admission and study arrangements are separate from its Hosur medical campus.
universities.campusLifestyle: The Avadi campus has academic departments, laboratories, a library and sports facilities. The engineering curriculum combines classroom subjects with practical and project-based learning. Student activities include NSS, NCC, clubs and sports; the exact combination of academic and practical work depends on the chosen award.
universities.cityProfile: The Chennai campus is at Avadi, Chennai 600054. Confirm the Avadi teaching location on your admission record before booking accommodation or planning a commute. The university’s Hosur medical campus and Bengaluru off-campus offerings have separate locations and admission arrangements.
universities.practicalExposure: The 2025 engineering regulations provide for theory, practical or laboratory-integrated courses, internships and project work. The standard B.Tech. route has eight semesters over four years. Admission by lateral entry or credit transfer has separate rules and should not be treated as the first-semester school-leaver route.
universities.hostelOverview: The university provides separate men’s and women’s hostels. Its admission policy describes single, double and dormitory occupancy. Request current room availability, allotment conditions, residence rules and a complete hostel quotation before arranging your move; the Chennai engineering academic fee table does not establish a hostel budget.
universities.dietarySupport: The university’s admission policy describes subsidised food support. Confirm the current meal plan, mess charges and any dietary requirements directly before accepting accommodation. Food and residence charges need separate budgeting alongside the programme’s academic payment.
universities.safetyOverview: The campus has a health centre and an ambulance facility, alongside anti-ragging, grievance and Internal Complaints Cell arrangements. Students can use the university’s grievance routes for admission or campus concerns. These facilities do not replace individual medical or fitness assessment required for a particular programme.
universities.studentSupport: Students have library, counselling and academic support arrangements. The admission policy provides screening, counselling, document verification and registration through the admission office. International applicants need a separate assessment of qualification equivalence, English proficiency and category-specific charges through the Office of International Relations.

faq.question: Is SPIHER a deemed-to-be university?
faq.answer: UGC lists St. Peter’s Institute of Higher Education and Research at Chennai as a deemed-to-be university established in 2008. The Avadi institution is distinct from similarly named affiliated colleges.

faq.question: Where do these engineering programmes take place?
faq.answer: These regular B.Tech. routes are at Avadi, Chennai 600054. Check the teaching campus on your admission record; Hosur medical programmes and Bengaluru off-campus routes are separate.

faq.question: How long is regular B.Tech. study?
faq.answer: The first-semester route takes four academic years across eight semesters. Lateral entry and credit-transfer rules are separate and may change the entry semester.

faq.question: What is the teaching language?
faq.answer: The 2025-onwards engineering regulations specify English for instruction, examinations and project reports. Courses in other languages are exceptions.

faq.question: What school qualification is required?
faq.answer: Applicants need the 10+2 Higher Secondary Examination in the academic stream or an institution-accepted equivalent. Obtain the exact programme-specific subject, marks, attempt and fitness conditions before applying.

faq.question: Is an entrance examination required?
faq.answer: The engineering regulations require the entrance examination prescribed by the institution. It tests eligible subjects at 10+2 academic-stream standard; confirm the next cycle’s format and schedule.

faq.question: Can I use a foreign school qualification?
faq.answer: Foreign qualifications need separate equivalence and admission assessment. The university’s international policy refers to the Office of International Relations, English proficiency and separately prescribed fees; programme-specific acceptance needs confirmation.

faq.question: When did the 2026 first-year classes begin?
faq.answer: The Chennai academic calendar scheduled UG first-year classes to commence on 15 July 2026. This is a historical cycle date; applicants to a future cycle need a fresh admission notice and start confirmation.

faq.question: Does the fee table give tuition alone?

faq.question: Are hostels available?
faq.answer: The university has separate men’s and women’s hostels and describes single, double and dormitory occupancy. Confirm allotment, current charges and residence rules before arranging travel.

faq.question: What practical study does B.Tech. include?
faq.answer: The engineering regulations include practical or laboratory-integrated courses, internships and project work alongside theory. The exact subjects and assessment depend on the department and chosen engineering award.

faq.question: How do the degree and honours pathways differ?
faq.answer: Faculty regulations provide a bachelor degree after three years and an honours or research honours award after a fourth year, subject to completion conditions. The current specialised BCA Data Science and AI/ML routes shown here are four-year honours awards.

faq.question: Do Arts and Science courses all have the same entry rules?
faq.answer: No. The faculty annexure specifies different school-subject routes for economics, business, commerce, sciences and computing. Some computing subjects are expressed as preferences; Microbiology applicants outside the Biology, Physics and Chemistry route need an individual assessment.

St. Peter’s Institute of Higher Education and Research is a private deemed-to-be university at Avadi, Chennai. Its academic portfolio spans engineering, architecture, arts, sciences, commerce and management. Regular engineering degrees combine classroom study with practical, internship and project work. Chennai admission and study arrangements are separate from its Hosur medical campus.

The Avadi campus has academic departments, laboratories, a library and sports facilities. The engineering curriculum combines classroom subjects with practical and project-based learning. Student activities include NSS, NCC, clubs and sports; the exact combination of academic and practical work depends on the chosen award.

The Chennai campus is at Avadi, Chennai 600054. Confirm the Avadi teaching location on your admission record before booking accommodation or planning a commute. The university’s Hosur medical campus and Bengaluru off-campus offerings have separate locations and admission arrangements.

The 2025 engineering regulations provide for theory, practical or laboratory-integrated courses, internships and project work. The standard B.Tech. route has eight semesters over four years. Admission by lateral entry or credit transfer has separate rules and should not be treated as the first-semester school-leaver route.

The university provides separate men’s and women’s hostels. Its admission policy describes single, double and dormitory occupancy. Request current room availability, allotment conditions, residence rules and a complete hostel quotation before arranging your move; the Chennai engineering academic fee table does not establish a hostel budget.

The university’s admission policy describes subsidised food support. Confirm the current meal plan, mess charges and any dietary requirements directly before accepting accommodation. Food and residence charges need separate budgeting alongside the programme’s academic payment.

The campus has a health centre and an ambulance facility, alongside anti-ragging, grievance and Internal Complaints Cell arrangements. Students can use the university’s grievance routes for admission or campus concerns. These facilities do not replace individual medical or fitness assessment required for a particular programme.

Students have library, counselling and academic support arrangements. The admission policy provides screening, counselling, document verification and registration through the admission office. International applicants need a separate assessment of qualification equivalence, English proficiency and category-specific charges through the Office of International Relations.
